section_path: 6 The philosophy of the scale-free network

note:
Fourteen measured regions over twelve of twenty-one pages, all accounted for, no refusals: eleven figure rows and three tables. The paper numbers eleven figures and seven tables and never mixes the two - every figure caption prints below its art and every table caption above its grid. Two grids print their header twice because they are two blocks side by side inside one frame (Tables 5 and 6), so both carry the physical column count.

Unmeasured, declared rather than invented: Table 1 on p3, Table 2 on p8, Table 3 on p9 and Table 7 on p18 all print as two-rule booktabs grids, and the two rules of each stand 314.1, 178.7, 178.5 and 180.4 pt apart, past the 120 pt grouping gap, so the layout pass never clusters them - and the table-tail fallback cannot either, because it seeds its window from a rule's own bottom edge and a stroked rule has zero height. Table 1 is the symbol table, 2 columns with three centred bold group rows merged across both, rule under the header and closing rule, 316.9 pt or 76 per cent of the measure. Table 2 is 4 columns over 15 ranks ('Ranking', 'D_C(x)', 'ID', 'Name of authors'), 336.9 pt or 80 per cent. Table 3 is 4 columns over 15 ranks ('Ranking', 'E value', 'ID', 'Name of authors'), 334.9 pt or 80 per cent, and its rank 1 value prints 0.26 against 0.234, 0.209 everywhere else. Table 7 is 3 columns over 15 stars ('Name', 'PR value', 'Google search results(million)'), 321.7 pt or 77 per cent, and it is the table Figure 9's abscissa is taken from.

Defects recorded, not corrected: Figure 2 labels two of its three axes 'Normalization Degree Centrality', so one label is wrong; Figure 3's caption promises a power-law distribution while both axes are linear, so the -1.6 exponent the prose quotes has nothing to sit on; Figure 7 carries Figure 4's caption verbatim ('directed citation network') over a co-star network of actors, and its 'Toby Maguire' label misspells Tobey; Figure 8 prints 'PageRank=1' with no spaces and mixes two stroke weights between arrows of the same panel; Figure 6's dashed quadrant divider at y 3.4 prints faint enough to disappear in reproduction and its callout arrow points at the box rather than at the node; Table 4 halves its caption into title case with no closing stop, and four impact factors repeat across different papers because two papers share a journal; Table 5 truncates its values to four or five decimals with five ties printed as identical strings and no tie mark; Table 6's right block runs 11.0, 0.5, 3.125, out of order; every use of 'MATLAB@2012b' on the page should be a registered mark; and the prose typos stand as printed: 'The Citation net- work', 'network(as is shown in Figure 7)', 'Strogatz.S.', 'Watts,D.'.
rules: a numbered table whose two rules stand 180 pt apart is measured by no region at all, so four of the seven tables in this paper are declared gaps instead of receiving an invented bbox [table.rule_style]
a grid drawn as two side-by-side blocks inside one ruled frame is one table: cols counts the physical columns and the header band prints twice [table.cols]
horizontal rules with one full-height centre divider and no side verticals are booktabs, not vertical-rules and not boxed, because no cell is closed [table.rule_style]
a band of two alternating rows - an ID row over its value row, three times - is six printed rows and one header row, not three rows [table.rows]
a grid set short of the measure keeps width full: 74 to 88 per cent of the local 419.4 pt measure is a wide table with air around it, and the percentage is named in the note [table.width]

the measured box is not the exhibit: Table 5's region stops at 564.1 pt while its closing rule prints at 589.6 pt, and the record keeps the measured bbox with the shortfall in the note [table.note_sentence]

a caption printed above the grid belongs to that grid even when the previous exhibit's caption printed below its art: the side follows the exhibit type, and this paper splits cleanly - figures below, tables above [caption.position]

a numbered caption that names the wrong subject is recorded as printed and the mismatch goes into the item note; Figure 7 carries Figure 4's caption word for word over a different network [caption.verbatim]
a 3-D scatter drawn in a dashed perspective box is scatter with three_d isometric, not surface-or-3D, because the axes hold point markers and no mesh [geometry.three_d]
two panels of the same family print as one row with panel_count 2, and only exhibits whose panels differ in family become composite-panel [geometry.panel_count]
printed_numbers is about the axes: a scatter whose ticks print 0.5 to 4.5 carries them, while the illustration that follows has no scale at all [geometry.printed_numbers]
an exhibit the prose never numbers is still a row when it fills the page slot - Figure 5 is introduced as 'the equation above' and Figure 11 as nothing at all [mention.count]
a figure cited a page or two BEFORE it prints carries a negative lead_pages, and the value is the exhibit page minus the citing page, never an absolute [mention.lead_pages]

a heading printed below the art can still govern the page, but here every path is the printed label of the heading that actually governs the region, so section_numbered is true throughout except the unnumbered reference list [place.section_numbered]
a legend pasted into the plot area counts as legend inside, and an annotation box with an arrow is not a legend: Figure 6 keys nothing and carries legend none [geometry.legend]
